Scientists have developed catalyst X, which converts the toxic gas CO to CO_2 under the action of D. Its formula mass is approximately 471.5, and its structure is shown below, where P represents a P(tBu)_2 group. Write the d-orbital electron configuration of the metal ion in X in an octahedral field, approximating the geometry as a regular octahedron.

Label D denotes $N_2O$.
Based on experimental observations, the following principal catalytic pathway has been proposed: X reacts with D to form Y, whose formula mass is approximately 487.5. Y rapidly converts into its more stable isomer Z. Z then takes up one molecule of CO while releasing one molecule of CO_2, regenerating X. Write the SMILES structures of Y and Z.
rubric: Z: 'CC(C)([P]1(C=C2N(C(C3=CC=CC=[N]34)=CC=C2)[Ru]14(C(O)=O)C#O)C(C)(C)C)C' (2 points). Stereochemistry is not required.

subquestions.text_open: The scientists also found that when THF is used as the solvent, another pathway may operate: X slowly isomerizes to isomer W, which contains two aromatic rings, and W then catalyzes exactly the same process as X. Write the SMILES structure of W.
